scope: Every original source file: 325 unique SHA-256 contents and 462 paths. Individual static/variant, current-path, bounded native execution and checksum-mode audit. This is not a declaration that every game/utility works completely.
coverage_limits: No full playthrough, all endings, all sound effects, all saves or physical-board schematic claim.
Unsupported external hardware remains: Art Tool Sega Loader Board/host link and Magistr16 enhanced platform.

Rows/checkpoints and native CPU values are actual observations. Selected bus ports are samples; omitted direct ROM/RAM accesses and capped noisy handlers prevent universal negative conclusions.

smw64.control_flow: The original Z80 driver writes mode 1 and data 5A, then expects 5A/5B at 660005/660007. Those bytes are only compared. The success path overwrites A and initializes Z80 RAM091B=B7,091C=02; the failure path would choose 60/1B. F2 changes both JR NZ displacements to zero in both copies of the routine, so open-bus FF still falls through to exactly the success path. F1 removes the protection setup and also uses B7/02 directly.
smw64.runtime_evidence: Existing 1200-frame traces observe original native responses5A/5B and f2 open busFF/FF. New read-only 20-frame Z80 probes show B7/02 in all three variants at frames16,17,20. No register values were injected and no ROM/state was changed.
smw64.sound_resource_evidence: The entire upper512KiB differs between original and f2 by only the four bypass-displacement bytes. Other sound driver/data bytes, including success initialization constants and all bytesD0000..FFFFF, are identical.
smw64.conclusion: No missing sound/protection hardware is established for f2. Existing native hardware should remain confined to original; assigning it to a linear software fix is unjustified. PCM timing differences are not treated as sound quality proof. No core edits performed.
